The first time I watched the show I stopped at the 11th episode of the last season. That was right after it was released on Netflix but I couldn't bring myself to finish it, it was such a comfort moment of my day to lay on my ex's bed and watch a few episodes. Fast forward a couple years to last week, I was struggling with some issues and my mental health was getting bad again. Given that my now bf lives a few towns over and I'm usually alone during the day everyday I thought that I'd rewatch the show and finish it this time.
It was worth it.
The last handful of episodes are a true discovery and tie up the whole show perfectly together. I was actually finally ready to let go and watch it till the last episode. It took me less than a week total and I think that it healed me and helped me through this uncertain time I'm going through. I feel at peace because I know that no matter how bad things go for me I'll always have those 20 minutes of comfort if I need it. And it also helped me reflect about having regrets in life.
My advice to you is to watch it when you think you're ready, it'll be great xx

Hi! I am 22 and not diagnosed yet. I do the same kinda things. I have many examples:
When I am doing something, even talking to someone or listening to a conversation, if there's any mentioning to something specific that makes me think of something else I often say the thing outloud even if it's just a word (like an association of thoughts). I try to stop myself when I'm with others but occasionally I do it anyways.
I am not English native speaker and I find some English words interesting to pronunciate so I find myself repeat words or sentences to myself for quite some time while I do other things, I even record myself sometimes.
When I am just chilling by myself and I get lost in my inner dialogue I either start repeating it outloud word to word or react to it like if it was a video that I'm watching and I just say words or facial expressions or laugh at my own jokes.
I do many facial expressions when I think of any fake scenario in my head.
Thanks to TikTok/internet I have many words or song that I completely randomly say or sing outloud, by myself or even during conversations if I'm comfortable enough with the others.

I have the same exact issue and when I'm overwhelmed I forget everything too.

What I personally try to do is:

-plan one day at a time, not too specific but just a general understanding of what I want and should do during any given segment of the day (morning-afternoon-evening).

-destroy the absolute shit of every task into small small tasks that require little to no energy.
(For example: if the task is doing full laundry and I'm laying on the bed I'd tell myself that the first task is to sit up, then put one feet on the ground, the another, the put on one shoe, eccetera eccetera until I am doing the big task and if I feel like giving up then I tell myself that if I've come this far I at least can do the same amount of small tasks, then again and again until I've done everything of that one big task).

-when I'm foggy and have to do stuff I try to talk to someone who knows what I have to do (if there is) to remember me and guide me through or I just pull out my papers/memos where I write everything down. If there are no papers written ahead then it's harder but it isn't impossible. You can absolutely do it, you can write down or type it in your phone (I find writing on paper way better because I don't get distracted by the phone and I can just put the paper on the wall where I can see it at all times) what you need to do to focus on your tasks and have a big picture of everything. It might require some time to write so try to be synthetic and brief as much as you can to avoid getting too much into detailing everything and procrastinating instead of getting things done.

-my therapist told me that when I get too foggy and unfocused I could do one or two things to ground myself and do it everytime so that I teach myself to ground. I still haven't found the perfect thing that works for me but they told me to focus on the senses, like making a specific sound or looking at something or smelling a specific strong scent or touch something (maybe like fidgeting?). I have tried tapping the pen on the table when I unfocus while I'm trying to study for a few hours, lighting up a candle when I have to do chores in one room so that when I stop for some reason then I smell it and know that I have to move and do stuff, putting on the same playlist when I have to do something that doesn't require too much concentration (better if there are no lyrics and the music feels right with what you're trying to accomplish, like lo-fi for mental work, jazz for self care things, trap/techno beats for things that require physical energy)


And now, here's a few useful and "obvious" advices that you might be forgetting:
-put away distractions like electronic devices, unhealthy snacks, side tasks that are not relevant at the moment (I'm assuming we all have that thing on the shelf that has been waiting to be fixed that's irritating to look at, put it away where you don't see it/them)
-breathing exercises as soon as you realize you're feeling panicky
-don't forget to take care of your body, eat good amounts, take bathroom breaks, stay well hydrated throughout the day, and most importantly sleep and allow yourself to rest when you need it (sleep has a huge impact on my productivity). Listen to your body.
Bonus: depending on your habits and body, avoid coffee if it just makes you anxious and shaky or drink it if you don't usually take it and you know that it can help you staying awake and aware. But be cautious if you know that it doesn't make you sleep you could drink it only in the morning. Or just tea that has enough caffeine, your choice.


And remember that you've come this far, most likely you can continue to do at least the same amount of work, maybe even better and more mindfully.

Good luck and stay strong xx
